personae.name: MISTRESS ANNE PAGE
personae.blurb: her daughter, in love with Fenton

lines.text: Enter Justice Shallow, Slender and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Sir Hugh, persuade me not. I will make a Star Chamber matter of it. If

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: he were twenty Sir John Falstaffs, he shall not abuse Robert Shallow,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: esquire.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: In the county of Gloucester, Justice of Peace and Coram.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ay, cousin Slender, and Custalorum.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, and Ratolorum too; and a gentleman born, Master Parson, who writes

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: himself “Armigero” in any bill, warrant, quittance, or

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: obligation—“Armigero.”

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ay, that I do, and have done any time these three hundred years.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: All his successors, gone before him hath done’t; and all his ancestors

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: that come after him may. They may give the dozen white luces in their

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: coat.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: It is an old coat.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: The dozen white louses do become an old coat well. It agrees well,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: passant. It is a familiar beast to man, and signifies love.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: The luce is the fresh fish. The salt fish is an old coat.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I may quarter, coz.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: You may, by marrying.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is marring indeed, if he quarter it.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Not a whit.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Yes, py’r Lady. If he has a quarter of your coat, there is but three

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: skirts for yourself, in my simple conjectures. But that is all one. If

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Sir John Falstaff have committed disparagements unto you, I am of the

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Church, and will be glad to do my benevolence to make atonements and

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: compremises between you.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: The Council shall hear it; it is a riot.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is not meet the Council hear a riot. There is no fear of Got in a

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: riot. The Council, look you, shall desire to hear the fear of Got, and

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: not to hear a riot. Take your vizaments in that.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ha! O’ my life, if I were young again, the sword should end it.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is petter that friends is the sword, and end it; and there is also

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: another device in my prain, which peradventure prings goot discretions

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: with it. There is Anne Page, which is daughter to Master George Page,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: which is pretty virginity.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Mistress Anne Page? She has brown hair, and speaks small like a woman?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is that fery person for all the ’orld, as just as you will desire,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: and seven hundred pounds of moneys, and gold, and silver, is her

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: grandsire upon his death’s-bed—Got deliver to a joyful

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: resurrections!—give, when she is able to overtake seventeen years old.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It were a goot motion if we leave our pribbles and prabbles, and desire

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: a marriage between Master Abraham and Mistress Anne Page.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Did her grandsire leave her seven hundred pound?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Ay, and her father is make her a petter penny.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I know the young gentlewoman; she has good gifts.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Seven hundred pounds, and possibilities, is goot gifts.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Well, let us see honest Master Page. Is Falstaff there?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Shall I tell you a lie? I do despise a liar as I do despise one that is

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: false, or as I despise one that is not true. The knight Sir John is

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: there, and I beseech you be ruled by your well-willers. I will peat the

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: door for Master Page.
[_Knocks._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: What, ho! Got pless your house here!
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Who’s there?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Here is Got’s plessing, and your friend, and Justice Shallow, and here

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: young Master Slender, that peradventures shall tell you another tale,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: if matters grow to your likings.
Enter Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I am glad to see your worships well. I thank you for my venison, Master

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Master Page, I am glad to see you, much good do it your good heart! I

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: wished your venison better; it was ill killed. How doth good Mistress

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Page? And I thank you always with my heart, la, with my heart.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Sir, I thank you.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Sir, I thank you; by yea and no, I do.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I am glad to see you, good Master Slender.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: How does your fallow greyhound, sir? I heard say he was outrun on

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Cotsall.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: It could not be judged, sir.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: You’ll not confess, you’ll not confess.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: That he will not. ’Tis your fault; ’tis your fault. ’Tis a good dog.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: A cur, sir.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Sir, he’s a good dog, and a fair dog, can there be more said? He is

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: good, and fair. Is Sir John Falstaff here?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Sir, he is within; and I would I could do a good office between you.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is spoke as a Christians ought to speak.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: He hath wronged me, Master Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Sir, he doth in some sort confess it.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: If it be confessed, it is not redressed. Is not that so, Master Page?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: He hath wronged me, indeed he hath, at a word, he hath. Believe me.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Robert Shallow, esquire, saith he is wronged.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Here comes Sir John.
Enter Sir John Falstaff, Bardolph, Nym and Pistol.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now, Master Shallow, you’ll complain of me to the King?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Knight, you have beaten my men, killed my deer, and broke open my

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: lodge.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But not kissed your keeper’s daughter!

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Tut, a pin! This shall be answered.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I will answer it straight: I have done all this. That is now answered.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: The Council shall know this.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’Twere better for you if it were known in counsel: you’ll be laughed

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: at.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: _Pauca verba_, Sir John; goot worts.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Good worts? Good cabbage!—Slender, I broke your head. What matter have

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: you against me?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Marry, sir, I have matter in my head against you, and against your

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: cony-catching rascals, Bardolph, Nym, and Pistol. They carried me to

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: the tavern and made me drunk, and afterwards picked my pocket.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: You Banbury cheese!

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, it is no matter.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: How now, Mephostophilus?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, it is no matter.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Slice, I say! _Pauca, pauca_, slice, that’s my humour.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Where’s Simple, my man? Can you tell, cousin?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Peace, I pray you. Now let us understand; there is three umpires in

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: this matter, as I understand: that is, Master Page, _fidelicet_ Master

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Page; and there is myself, _fidelicet_ myself; and the three party is,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: lastly and finally, mine host of the Garter.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: We three to hear it and end it between them.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Fery goot. I will make a prief of it in my notebook, and we will

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: afterwards ’ork upon the cause with as great discreetly as we can.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Pistol!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: He hears with ears.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: The tevil and his tam! What phrase is this, “He hears with ear”? Why,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: it is affectations.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Pistol, did you pick Master Slender’s purse?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, by these gloves, did he, or I would I might never come in mine own

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: great chamber again else! Of seven groats in mill-sixpences, and two

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Edward shovel-boards that cost me two shilling and two pence a-piece of

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Yed Miller, by these gloves.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Is this true, Pistol?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: No, it is false, if it is a pick-purse.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Ha, thou mountain-foreigner!—Sir John and master mine,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I combat challenge of this latten bilbo.—

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Word of denial in thy _labras_ here!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Word of denial! Froth and scum, thou liest.
[_Points at Nym_.]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: By these gloves, then, ’twas he.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: Be avised, sir, and pass good humours. I will say “marry trap with

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: you”, if you run the nuthook’s humour on me. That is the very note of

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: it.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: By this hat, then, he in the red face had it. For though I cannot

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: remember what I did when you made me drunk, yet I am not altogether an

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: ass.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What say you, Scarlet and John?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Why, sir, for my part, I say the gentleman had drunk himself out of his

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: five sentences.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is his “five senses”. Fie, what the ignorance is!

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: And being fap, sir, was, as they say, cashiered; and so conclusions

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: passed the careers.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, you spake in Latin then too; but ’tis no matter. I’ll ne’er be

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: drunk whilst I live again, but in honest, civil, godly company, for

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: this trick. If I be drunk, I’ll be drunk with those that have the fear

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: of God, and not with drunken knaves.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: So Got ’udge me, that is a virtuous mind.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You hear all these matters denied, gentlemen; you hear it.
Enter Mistress Ford, Mistress Page and her daughter Anne Page with wine.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Nay, daughter, carry the wine in, we’ll drink within.
[_Exit Anne Page._]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: O heaven, this is Mistress Anne Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: How now, Mistress Ford?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mistress Ford, by my troth, you are very well met. By your leave, good

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: mistress.
[_Kisses her._]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Wife, bid these gentlemen welcome. Come, we have a hot venison pasty to

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: dinner. Come, gentlemen, I hope we shall drink down all unkindness.
[_Exeunt all but Slender._]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I had rather than forty shillings I had my book of _Songs and Sonnets_

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: here.
Enter Simple.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: How now, Simple, where have you been? I must wait on myself, must I?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: You have not the _Book of Riddles_ about you, have you?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: _Book of Riddles?_ Why, did you not lend it to Alice Shortcake upon

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Allhallowmas last, a fortnight afore Michaelmas?
Enter Shallow and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Come, coz; come, coz, we stay for you. A word with you, coz. Marry,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: this, coz: there is, as ’twere, a tender, a kind of tender, made afar

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: off by Sir Hugh here. Do you understand me?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, sir, you shall find me reasonable. If it be so, I shall do that

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: that is reason.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Nay, but understand me.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: So I do, sir.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Give ear to his motions, Master Slender. I will description the matter

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: to you, if you be capacity of it.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Nay, I will do as my cousin Shallow says. I pray you pardon me, he’s a

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Justice of Peace in his country, simple though I stand here.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: But that is not the question. The question is concerning your marriage.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ay, there’s the point, sir.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Marry, is it; the very point of it—to Mistress Anne Page.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Why, if it be so, I will marry her upon any reasonable demands.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: But can you affection the ’oman? Let us command to know that of your

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: mouth, or of your lips; for divers philosophers hold that the lips is

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: parcel of the mouth. Therefore, precisely, can you carry your good will

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: to the maid?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Cousin Abraham Slender, can you love her?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I hope, sir, I will do as it shall become one that would do reason.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Nay, Got’s lords and his ladies! You must speak possitable, if you can

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: carry her your desires towards her.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: That you must. Will you, upon good dowry, marry her?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I will do a greater thing than that, upon your request, cousin, in any

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: reason.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Nay, conceive me, conceive me, sweet coz. What I do is to pleasure you,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: coz. Can you love the maid?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I will marry her, sir, at your request. But if there be no great love

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: in the beginning, yet heaven may decrease it upon better acquaintance,

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: when we are married and have more occasion to know one another. I hope

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: upon familiarity will grow more contempt. But if you say “Marry her,” I

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: will marry her. That I am freely dissolved, and dissolutely.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is a fery discretion answer, save the fall is in the ’ord

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: “dissolutely.” The ’ort is, according to our meaning, “resolutely.” His

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: meaning is good.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Ay, I think my cousin meant well.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, or else I would I might be hanged, la!

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Here comes fair Mistress Anne.
Enter Anne Page.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Here comes fair Mistress Anne.—Would I were young for your sake,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Mistress Anne.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: The dinner is on the table, my father desires your worships’ company.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I will wait on him, fair Mistress Anne.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: ’Od’s plessed will! I will not be absence at the grace.
[_Exeunt Shallow and Sir Hugh Evans._]

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Will’t please your worship to come in, sir?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: No, I thank you, forsooth, heartily; I am very well.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: The dinner attends you, sir.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I am not a-hungry, I thank you, forsooth. [_To Simple_.] Go, sirrah,

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: for all you are my man, go wait upon my cousin Shallow.
[_Exit Simple._]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: A Justice of Peace sometime may be beholding to his friend for a man. I

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: keep but three men and a boy yet, till my mother be dead. But what

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: though? Yet I live like a poor gentleman born.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I may not go in without your worship. They will not sit till you come.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I’ faith, I’ll eat nothing. I thank you as much as though I did.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I pray you, sir, walk in.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I had rather walk here, I thank you. I bruised my shin th’ other day

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: with playing at sword and dagger with a master of fence—three veneys

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: for a dish of stewed prunes—and, by my troth, I cannot abide the smell

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: of hot meat since. Why do your dogs bark so? Be there bears i’ the

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: town?

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I think there are, sir; I heard them talked of.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I love the sport well, but I shall as soon quarrel at it as any man in

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: England. You are afraid, if you see the bear loose, are you not?

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Ay, indeed, sir.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: That’s meat and drink to me now. I have seen Sackerson loose twenty

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: times, and have taken him by the chain. But, I warrant you, the women

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: have so cried and shrieked at it that it passed. But women, indeed,

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: cannot abide ’em; they are very ill-favoured rough things.
Enter Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Come, gentle Master Slender, come. We stay for you.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I’ll eat nothing, I thank you, sir.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: By cock and pie, you shall not choose, sir! Come, come.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Nay, pray you lead the way.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Come on, sir.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Mistress Anne, yourself shall go first.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Not I, sir; pray you keep on.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Truly, I will not go first; truly, la! I will not do you that wrong.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I pray you, sir.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I’ll rather be unmannerly than troublesome. You do yourself wrong,

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: indeed, la!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Hugh Evans and Simple.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Go your ways, and ask of Doctor Caius’ house which is the way. And

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: there dwells one Mistress Quickly, which is in the manner of his nurse,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: or his dry nurse, or his cook, or his laundry, his washer and his

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: wringer.

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Well, sir.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Nay, it is petter yet. Give her this letter. For it is a ’oman that

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: altogether’s acquaintance with Mistress Anne Page; and the letter is to

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: desire and require her to solicit your master’s desires to Mistress

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Anne Page. I pray you be gone. I will make an end of my dinner; there’s

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: pippins and cheese to come.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A room in the Garter Inn

lines.text: Enter Falstaff, Host, Bardolph, Nym, Pistol and Robin.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mine host of the Garter!

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: What says my bully rook? Speak scholarly and wisely.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Truly, mine host, I must turn away some of my followers.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Discard, bully Hercules; cashier. Let them wag; trot, trot.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I sit at ten pounds a week.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Thou’rt an emperor—Caesar, Keiser, and Pheazar. I will entertain

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Bardolph. He shall draw, he shall tap. Said I well, bully Hector?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Do so, good mine host.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: I have spoke, let him follow.—Let me see thee froth and lime. I am at a

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: word, follow.
[_Exit Host._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bardolph, follow him. A tapster is a good trade. An old cloak makes a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: new jerkin; a withered servingman a fresh tapster. Go, adieu.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: It is a life that I have desired. I will thrive.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: O base Hungarian wight, wilt thou the spigot wield?
[_Exit Bardolph._]

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: He was gotten in drink. Is not the humour conceited?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I am glad I am so acquit of this tinderbox. His thefts were too open.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: His filching was like an unskilful singer, he kept not time.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: The good humour is to steal at a minute’s rest.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: “Convey,” the wise it call. “Steal?” Foh! A _fico_ for the phrase!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, sirs, I am almost out at heels.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Why, then, let kibes ensue.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: There is no remedy, I must cony-catch, I must shift.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Young ravens must have food.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Which of you know Ford of this town?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I ken the wight, he is of substance good.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: My honest lads, I will tell you what I am about.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Two yards, and more.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No quips now, Pistol. Indeed, I am in the waist two yards about, but I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: am now about no waste; I am about thrift. Briefly, I do mean to make

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: love to Ford’s wife. I spy entertainment in her. She discourses, she

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: carves, she gives the leer of invitation. I can construe the action of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: her familiar style; and the hardest voice of her behaviour, to be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Englished rightly, is “I am Sir John Falstaff’s.”

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: He hath studied her will and translated her will—out of honesty into

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: English.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: The anchor is deep. Will that humour pass?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now, the report goes she has all the rule of her husband’s purse. He

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hath a legion of angels.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: As many devils entertain, and “To her, boy,” say I.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: The humour rises; it is good. Humour me the angels.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I have writ me here a letter to her; and here another to Page’s wife,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: who even now gave me good eyes too, examined my parts with most

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: judicious oeillades. Sometimes the beam of her view gilded my foot,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sometimes my portly belly.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Then did the sun on dunghill shine.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I thank thee for that humour.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: O, she did so course o’er my exteriors with such a greedy intention

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that the appetite of her eye did seem to scorch me up like a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: burning-glass. Here’s another letter to her. She bears the purse too;

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: she is a region in Guiana, all gold and bounty. I will be cheaters to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: them both, and they shall be exchequers to me; they shall be my East

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and West Indies, and I will trade to them both. Go, bear thou this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: letter to Mistress Page;—and thou this to Mistress Ford. We will

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thrive, lads, we will thrive.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Shall I Sir Pandarus of Troy become,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And by my side wear steel? Then Lucifer take all!

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I will run no base humour. Here, take the humour-letter. I will keep

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: the ’haviour of reputation.
[_To Robin_.]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hold, sirrah, bear you these letters tightly;

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Sail like my pinnace to these golden shores.—

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Rogues, hence, avaunt! Vanish like hailstones, go!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Trudge, plod away o’ th’ hoof, seek shelter, pack!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Falstaff will learn the humour of this age:

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: French thrift, you rogues—myself and skirted page.
[_Exeunt Falstaff and Robin._]

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Let vultures gripe thy guts! For gourd and fullam holds,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And high and low beguile the rich and poor.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Tester I’ll have in pouch when thou shalt lack,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Base Phrygian Turk!

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I have operations in my head which be humours of revenge.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Wilt thou revenge?

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: By welkin and her star!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: With wit or steel?

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: With both the humours, I.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: I will discuss the humour of this love to Ford.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And I to Page shall eke unfold

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: How Falstaff, varlet vile,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: His dove will prove, his gold will hold,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: And his soft couch defile.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: My humour shall not cool. I will incense Ford to deal with poison, I

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: will possess him with yellowness, for the revolt of mine is dangerous.

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: That is my true humour.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Thou art the Mars of malcontents. I second thee. Troop on.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A room in Doctor Caius’s house

lines.text: Enter Mistress Quickly and Simple.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: What, John Rugby!
Enter Rugby.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I pray thee go to the casement, and see if you can see my master,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Master Doctor Caius, coming. If he do, i’ faith, and find anybody in

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: the house, here will be an old abusing of God’s patience and the King’s

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: English.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: I’ll go watch.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Go; and we’ll have a posset for’t soon at night, in faith, at the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: latter end of a sea-coal fire.
[_Exit Rugby._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: An honest, willing, kind fellow, as ever servant shall come in house

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: withal; and, I warrant you, no tell-tale nor no breed-bate. His worst

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: fault is that he is given to prayer; he is something peevish that way,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: but nobody but has his fault. But let that pass. Peter Simple you say

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: your name is?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Ay, for fault of a better.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: And Master Slender’s your master?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Ay, forsooth.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Does he not wear a great round beard, like a glover’s paring-knife?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: No, forsooth, he hath but a little wee face, with a little yellow

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: beard, a Cain-coloured beard.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: A softly-sprighted man, is he not?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Ay, forsooth. But he is as tall a man of his hands as any is between

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: this and his head. He hath fought with a warrener.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: How say you? O, I should remember him. Does he not hold up his head, as

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: it were, and strut in his gait?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Yes, indeed, does he.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Well, heaven send Anne Page no worse fortune! Tell Master Parson Evans

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I will do what I can for your master. Anne is a good girl, and I wish—
Enter Rugby.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: Out, alas! Here comes my master.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: We shall all be shent. Run in here, good young man, go into this

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: closet. He will not stay long.
[_Simple steps into the closet._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: What, John Rugby! John! What, John, I say! Go, John, go inquire for my

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: master. I doubt he be not well, that he comes not home.
[_Exit Rugby._]
[_Sings_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: _And down, down, adown-a, etc._
Enter Doctor Caius.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: CAIUS

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Vat is you sing? I do not like dese toys. Pray you, go and vetch me in

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: my closet _une boîtine verte_, a box, a green-a box. Do intend vat I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: speak? A green-a box.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Ay, forsooth, I’ll fetch it you.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I am glad he went not in himself. If he had found the young

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: man, he would have been horn-mad.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: _Fe, fe, fe fe! Ma foi, il fait fort chaud. Je m’en vais à la cour—la

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: grande affaire._

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Is it this, sir?

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: _Oui, mette-le au mon_ pocket. _Dépêche_, quickly—Vere is dat knave

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Rugby?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: What, John Rugby, John!
Enter Rugby.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: You are John Rugby, and you are Jack Rugby. Come, take-a your rapier,

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: and come after my heel to the court.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: ’Tis ready, sir, here in the porch.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By my trot, I tarry too long. ’Od’s me! _Qu’ay j’oublié?_ Dere is some

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: simples in my closet dat I vill not for the varld I shall leave behind.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Ay me, he’ll find the young man there, and be mad!

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: _O diable, diable!_ Vat is in my closet? Villainy! _Larron!_ [_Pulling

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Simple out_.] Rugby, my rapier!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Good master, be content.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Wherefore shall I be content-a?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: The young man is an honest man.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: What shall de honest man do in my closet? Dere is no honest man dat

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: shall come in my closet.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I beseech you, be not so phlegmatic. Hear the truth of it. He came of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: an errand to me from Parson Hugh.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Vell?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Ay, forsooth, to desire her to—

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Peace, I pray you.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Peace-a your tongue!—Speak-a your tale.

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: To desire this honest gentlewoman, your maid, to speak a good word to

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Mistress Anne Page for my master in the way of marriage.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: This is all, indeed, la! But I’ll ne’er put my finger in the fire, and

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: need not.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Sir Hugh send-a you?—Rugby, _baille_ me some paper.—Tarry you a

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: little-a while.
[_Writes._]
[_Aside to Simple_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I am glad he is so quiet. If he had been throughly

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: moved, you should have heard him so loud and so melancholy. But

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: notwithstanding, man, I’ll do you your master what good I can; and the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: very yea and the no is, the French doctor, my master—I may call him my

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: master, look you, for I keep his house, and I wash, wring, brew, bake,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: scour, dress meat and drink, make the beds, and do all myself—
[_Aside to Mistress Quickly_.]

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: ’Tis a great charge to come under one

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: body’s hand.
[_Aside to Simple_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Are you avised o’ that? You shall find it a great

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: charge, and to be up early and down late; but notwithstanding—to tell

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: you in your ear, I would have no words of it—my master himself is in

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: love with Mistress Anne Page; but notwithstanding that, I know Anne’s

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: mind. That’s neither here nor there.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: You jack’nape, give-a dis letter to Sir Hugh. By gar, it is a

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: shallenge. I will cut his troat in de park, and I will teach a scurvy

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: jackanape priest to meddle or make. You may be gone, it is not good you

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: tarry here.—By gar, I will cut all his two stones. By gar, he shall not

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: have a stone to throw at his dog.
[_Exit Simple._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Alas, he speaks but for his friend.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: It is no matter-a ver dat. Do not you tell-a me dat I shall have Anne

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Page for myself? By gar, I vill kill de Jack priest; and I have

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: appointed mine host of de Jarteer to measure our weapon. By gar, I will

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: myself have Anne Page.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Sir, the maid loves you, and all shall be well. We must give folks

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: leave to prate. What, the good-year!

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Rugby, come to the court with me. [_To Mistress Quickly_.] By gar, if I

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: have not Anne Page, I shall turn your head out of my door.—Follow my

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: heels, Rugby.
[_Exeunt Caius and Rugby._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: You shall have An—fool’s head of your own. No, I know Anne’s mind for

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: that. Never a woman in Windsor knows more of Anne’s mind than I do, nor

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: can do more than I do with her, I thank heaven.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Who’s within there, ho?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Who’s there, I trow? Come near the house, I pray you.
Enter Fenton.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: How now, good woman? How dost thou?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: The better, that it pleases your good worship to ask.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: What news? How does pretty Mistress Anne?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: In truth, sir, and she is pretty, and honest, and gentle; and one that

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: is your friend, I can tell you that by the way, I praise heaven for it.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Shall I do any good, think’st thou? Shall I not lose my suit?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Troth, sir, all is in His hands above. But notwithstanding, Master

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Fenton, I’ll be sworn on a book she loves you. Have not your worship a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: wart above your eye?

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Yes, marry, have I; what of that?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Well, thereby hangs a tale. Good faith, it is such another Nan! But, I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: detest, an honest maid as ever broke bread. We had an hour’s talk of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: that wart. I shall never laugh but in that maid’s company. But, indeed,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: she is given too much to allicholy and musing. But for you—well, go to.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Well, I shall see her today. Hold, there’s money for thee. Let me have

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: thy voice in my behalf. If thou seest her before me, commend me.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Will I? I’ faith, that we will! And I will tell your worship more of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: the wart the next time we have confidence, and of other wooers.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Well, farewell, I am in great haste now.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Farewell to your worship.
[_Exit Fenton._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Truly, an honest gentleman—but Anne loves him not, for I know Anne’s

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: mind as well as another does. Out upon ’t, what have I forgot?
[_Exit._]
Enter Mistress Page reading a letter.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What, have I scaped love-letters in the holiday-time of my beauty, and

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: am I now a subject for them? Let me see.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: _Ask me no reason why I love you, for though Love use Reason

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: for his precisian, he admits him not for his counsellor. You are not

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: young, no more am I. Go to, then, there’s sympathy. You are merry, so

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: am I. Ha, ha, then there’s more sympathy. You love sack, and so do I.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Would you desire better sympathy? Let it suffice thee, Mistress Page,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: at the least, if the love of soldier can suffice, that I love thee. I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: will not say, pity me—’tis not a soldier-like phrase—but I say love me.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: By me,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Thine own true knight,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: By day or night,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Or any kind of light,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: With all his might,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: For thee to fight,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: John Falstaff._

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What a Herod of Jewry is this! O wicked, wicked world! One that is

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: well-nigh worn to pieces with age, to show himself a young gallant!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What an unweighed behaviour hath this Flemish drunkard picked—with the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: devil’s name!—out of my conversation, that he dares in this manner

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: assay me? Why, he hath not been thrice in my company! What should I say

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: to him? I was then frugal of my mirth. Heaven forgive me! Why, I’ll

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: exhibit a bill in the parliament for the putting down of men. How shall

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I be revenged on him? For revenged I will be, as sure as his guts are

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: made of puddings.
Enter Mistress Ford.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Mistress Page! Trust me, I was going to your house.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And, trust me, I was coming to you. You look very ill.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Nay, I’ll ne’er believe that. I have to show to the contrary.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Faith, but you do, in my mind.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Well, I do, then. Yet I say I could show you to the contrary. O,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Mistress Page, give me some counsel.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What’s the matter, woman?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: O woman, if it were not for one trifling respect, I could come to such

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: honour!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Hang the trifle, woman; take the honour. What is it? Dispense with

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: trifles. What is it?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: If I would but go to hell for an eternal moment or so, I could be

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: knighted.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What? Thou liest! Sir Alice Ford! These knights will hack, and so thou

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: shouldst not alter the article of thy gentry.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: We burn daylight. Here, read, read. Perceive how I might be knighted. I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: shall think the worse of fat men as long as I have an eye to make

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: difference of men’s liking. And yet he would not swear; praised women’s

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: modesty; and gave such orderly and well-behaved reproof to all

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: uncomeliness that I would have sworn his disposition would have gone to

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: the truth of his words. But they do no more adhere and keep place

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: together than the Hundredth Psalm to the tune of “Greensleeves.” What

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: tempest, I trow, threw this whale, with so many tuns of oil in his

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: belly, ashore at Windsor? How shall I be revenged on him? I think the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: best way were to entertain him with hope, till the wicked fire of lust

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: have melted him in his own grease. Did you ever hear the like?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Letter for letter, but that the name of Page and Ford differs! To thy

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: great comfort in this mystery of ill opinions, here’s the twin brother

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: of thy letter. But let thine inherit first, for I protest mine never

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: shall. I warrant he hath a thousand of these letters, writ with blank

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: space for different names—sure, more, and these are of the second

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: edition. He will print them, out of doubt; for he cares not what he

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: puts into the press, when he would put us two. I had rather be a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: giantess and lie under Mount Pelion. Well, I will find you twenty

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: lascivious turtles ere one chaste man.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, this is the very same—the very hand, the very words. What doth he

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: think of us?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Nay, I know not. It makes me almost ready to wrangle with mine own

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: honesty. I’ll entertain myself like one that I am not acquainted

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: withal; for, sure, unless he know some strain in me that I know not

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: myself, he would never have boarded me in this fury.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: “Boarding” call you it? I’ll be sure to keep him above deck.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: So will I. If he come under my hatches, I’ll never to sea again. Let’s

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: be revenged on him. Let’s appoint him a meeting, give him a show of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: comfort in his suit, and lead him on with a fine-baited delay, till he

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: hath pawned his horses to mine host of the Garter.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Nay, I will consent to act any villainy against him that may not sully

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: the chariness of our honesty. O, that my husband saw this letter! It

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: would give eternal food to his jealousy.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Why, look where he comes; and my good man too. He’s as far from

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: jealousy as I am from giving him cause, and that, I hope, is an

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: unmeasurable distance.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: You are the happier woman.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Let’s consult together against this greasy knight. Come hither.
[_They retire._]
Enter Ford with Pistol, and Page with Nym.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: FORD

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Well, I hope it be not so.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Hope is a curtal dog in some affairs.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Sir John affects thy wife.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Why, sir, my wife is not young.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: He woos both high and low, both rich and poor,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Both young and old, one with another, Ford.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: He loves the gallimaufry. Ford, perpend.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Love my wife?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: With liver burning hot.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Prevent, or go thou like Sir Actaeon he,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: With Ringwood at thy heels.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: O, odious is the name!

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: What name, sir?

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: The horn, I say. Farewell.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Take heed, have open eye, for thieves do foot by night.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Take heed, ere summer comes, or cuckoo birds do sing.—

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Away, Sir Corporal Nym.—Believe it, Page, he speaks sense.
[_Exit Pistol._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I will be patient. I will find out this.
[_To Page_.]

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: And this is true, I like not the humour of lying. He hath

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: wronged me in some humours. I should have borne the humoured letter to

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: her; but I have a sword, and it shall bite upon my necessity. He loves

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: your wife; there’s the short and the long. My name is Corporal Nym. I

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: speak, and I avouch ’tis true. My name is Nym, and Falstaff loves your

lines.speaker: NYM
lines.text: wife. Adieu. I love not the humour of bread and cheese. Adieu.
[_Exit Nym._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: “The humour of it,” quoth ’a! Here’s a fellow frights

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: English out of his wits.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I will seek out Falstaff.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I never heard such a drawling, affecting rogue.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: If I do find it—well.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I will not believe such a Cataian, though the priest o’ the

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: town commended him for a true man.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: ’Twas a good sensible fellow—well.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Mistress Page and Mistress Ford come forward.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: How now, Meg?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Whither go you, George? Hark you.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: How now, sweet Frank, why art thou melancholy?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I melancholy? I am not melancholy. Get you home, go.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Faith, thou hast some crotchets in thy head now.—Will you go, Mistress

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Page?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Have with you. You’ll come to dinner, George?
[_Aside to Mistress Ford_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Look who comes yonder. She shall be our

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: messenger to this paltry knight.
[_Aside to Mistress Page_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Trust me, I thought on her. She’ll fit it.
Enter Mistress Quickly.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: You are come to see my daughter Anne?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Ay, forsooth. And, I pray, how does good Mistress Anne?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Go in with us and see. We’d have an hour’s talk with you.
[_Exeunt Mistress Page, Mistress Ford and Mistress Quickly._]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: How now, Master Ford?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: You heard what this knave told me, did you not?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Yes, and you heard what the other told me?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Do you think there is truth in them?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Hang ’em, slaves! I do not think the knight would offer it, but these

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: that accuse him in his intent towards our wives are a yoke of his

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: discarded men, very rogues, now they be out of service.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Were they his men?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Marry, were they.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I like it never the better for that. Does he lie at the Garter?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Ay, marry, does he. If he should intend this voyage toward my wife, I

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: would turn her loose to him; and what he gets more of her than sharp

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: words, let it lie on my head.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I do not misdoubt my wife, but I would be loath to turn them together.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: A man may be too confident. I would have nothing lie on my head. I

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: cannot be thus satisfied.
Enter Host.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Look where my ranting host of the Garter comes. There is either liquor

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: in his pate or money in his purse when he looks so merrily.—How now,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: mine host?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: How now, bully rook? Thou’rt a gentleman.—Cavaliero Justice, I say!
Enter Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I follow, mine host, I follow.—Good even and twenty, good Master Page.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Master Page, will you go with us? We have sport in hand.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Tell him, Cavaliero Justice; tell him, bully rook.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Sir, there is a fray to be fought between Sir Hugh the Welsh priest and

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Caius the French doctor.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Good mine host o’ the Garter, a word with you.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: What say’st thou, my bully rook?
[_Ford and the Host talk apart._]
[_To Page_.]

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Will you go with us to behold it? My merry host hath had

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: the measuring of their weapons, and, I think, hath appointed them

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: contrary places; for, believe me, I hear the parson is no jester. Hark,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I will tell you what our sport shall be.
[_Shallow and Page talk apart. Ford and the Host come forward._]

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Hast thou no suit against my knight, my guest cavaliero?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: None, I protest. But I’ll give you a pottle of burnt sack to give me

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: recourse to him, and tell him my name is Brook, only for a jest.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: My hand, bully. Thou shalt have egress and regress—said I well?—and thy

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: name shall be Brook. It is a merry knight. Will you go, myn-heers?

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Have with you, mine host.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I have heard the Frenchman hath good skill in his rapier.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Tut, sir, I could have told you more. In these times you stand on

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: distance—your passes, stoccadoes, and I know not what. ’Tis the heart,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Master Page; ’tis here, ’tis here. I have seen the time, with my long

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: sword I would have made you four tall fellows skip like rats.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Here, boys, here, here! Shall we wag?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Have with you. I had rather hear them scold than fight.
[_Exeunt Host, Shallow and Page._]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Though Page be a secure fool, and stands so firmly on his wife’s

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: frailty, yet I cannot put off my opinion so easily. She was in his

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: company at Page’s house, and what they made there I know not. Well, I

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: will look further into ’t, and I have a disguise to sound Falstaff. If

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I find her honest, I lose not my labour. If she be otherwise, ’tis

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: labour well bestowed.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: A room in the Garter Inn

lines.text: Enter Falstaff and Pistol.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I will not lend thee a penny.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Why then, the world’s mine oyster,

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Which I with sword will open.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Not a penny. I have been content, sir, you should lay my countenance to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: pawn; I have grated upon my good friends for three reprieves for you

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and your coach-fellow Nym, or else you had looked through the grate

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: like a gemini of baboons. I am damned in hell for swearing to gentlemen

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: my friends you were good soldiers and tall fellows. And when Mistress

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bridget lost the handle of her fan, I took ’t upon mine honour thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: hadst it not.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Didst not thou share? Hadst thou not fifteen pence?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Reason, you rogue, reason. Think’st thou I’ll endanger my soul gratis?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: At a word, hang no more about me, I am no gibbet for you. Go—a short

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: knife and a throng—to your manor of Pickt-hatch, go. You’ll not bear a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: letter for me, you rogue? You stand upon your honour! Why, thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: unconfinable baseness, it is as much as I can do to keep the terms of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: my honour precise. Ay, ay, I myself sometimes, leaving the fear of God

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: on the left hand, and hiding mine honour in my necessity, am fain to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shuffle, to hedge, and to lurch; and yet you, rogue, will ensconce your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: rags, your cat-a-mountain looks, your red-lattice phrases, and your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: bold beating oaths, under the shelter of your honour! You will not do

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: it! You!

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: I do relent. What wouldst thou more of man?
Enter Robin.

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: ROBIN

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Sir, here’s a woman would speak with you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let her approach.
Enter Mistress Quickly.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Give your worship good morrow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Good morrow, goodwife.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Not so, an’t please your worship.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Good maid, then.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I’ll be sworn, as my mother was, the first hour I was born.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I do believe the swearer. What with me?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Shall I vouchsafe your worship a word or two?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Two thousand, fair woman; and I’ll vouchsafe thee the hearing.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: There is one Mistress Ford, sir—I pray, come a little nearer this ways.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I myself dwell with Master Doctor Caius.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, on; Mistress Ford, you say—

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Your worship says very true. I pray your worship come a little nearer

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: this ways.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I warrant thee, nobody hears. Mine own people, mine own people.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Are they so? God bless them, and make them His servants!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, Mistress Ford, what of her?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Why, sir, she’s a good creature. Lord, Lord, your worship’s a wanton!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Well, heaven forgive you, and all of us, I pray!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mistress Ford, come, Mistress Ford.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Marry, this is the short and the long of it: you have brought her into

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: such a canaries as ’tis wonderful. The best courtier of them all, when

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: the court lay at Windsor, could never have brought her to such a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: canary. Yet there has been knights, and lords, and gentlemen, with

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: their coaches, I warrant you, coach after coach, letter after letter,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: gift after gift, smelling so sweetly, all musk, and so rushling, I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: warrant you, in silk and gold, and in such alligant terms, and in such

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: wine and sugar of the best and the fairest, that would have won any

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: woman’s heart; and I warrant you, they could never get an eye-wink of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: her. I had myself twenty angels given me this morning, but I defy all

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: angels in any such sort, as they say, but in the way of honesty. And, I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: warrant you, they could never get her so much as sip on a cup with the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: proudest of them all. And yet there has been earls—nay, which is more,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: pensioners—but, I warrant you, all is one with her.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But what says she to me? Be brief, my good she-Mercury.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Marry, she hath received your letter, for the which she thanks you a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: thousand times; and she gives you to notify that her husband will be

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: absence from his house between ten and eleven.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ten and eleven?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Ay, forsooth; and then you may come and see the picture, she says, that

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: you wot of. Master Ford, her husband, will be from home. Alas, the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: sweet woman leads an ill life with him. He’s a very jealousy man; she

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: leads a very frampold life with him, good heart.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ten and eleven. Woman, commend me to her; I will not fail her.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Why, you say well. But I have another messenger to your worship.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Mistress Page hath her hearty commendations to you too; and let me tell

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: you in your ear, she’s as fartuous a civil modest wife, and one, I tell

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: you, that will not miss you morning nor evening prayer, as any is in

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Windsor, whoe’er be the other; and she bade me tell your worship that

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: her husband is seldom from home, but she hopes there will come a time.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I never knew a woman so dote upon a man. Surely I think you have

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: charms, la! Yes, in truth.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Not I, I assure thee. Setting the attraction of my good parts aside, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have no other charms.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Blessing on your heart for ’t!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But, I pray thee, tell me this: has Ford’s wife and Page’s wife

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: acquainted each other how they love me?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: That were a jest indeed! They have not so little grace, I hope. That

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: were a trick indeed! But Mistress Page would desire you to send her

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: your little page, of all loves. Her husband has a marvellous infection

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: to the little page; and, truly, Master Page is an honest man. Never a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: wife in Windsor leads a better life than she does. Do what she will,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: say what she will, take all, pay all, go to bed when she list, rise

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: when she list, all is as she will, and truly she deserves it, for if

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: there be a kind woman in Windsor, she is one. You must send her your

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: page, no remedy.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Why, I will.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Nay, but do so then, and, look you, he may come and go between you

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: both; and in any case have a nay-word, that you may know one another’s

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: mind, and the boy never need to understand anything; for ’tis not good

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: that children should know any wickedness. Old folks, you know, have

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: discretion, as they say, and know the world.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Fare thee well, commend me to them both. There’s my purse; I am yet thy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: debtor. Boy, go along with this woman.—This news distracts me.
[_Exeunt Mistress Quickly and Robin._]

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: This punk is one of Cupid’s carriers;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Clap on more sails, pursue; up with your fights;

lines.speaker: PISTOL
lines.text: Give fire! She is my prize, or ocean whelm them all!
[_Exit Pistol._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Sayst thou so, old Jack? Go thy ways, I’ll make more of thy old body

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: than I have done. Will they yet look after thee? Wilt thou, after the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: expense of so much money, be now a gainer? Good body, I thank thee. Let

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: them say ’tis grossly done; so it be fairly done, no matter.
Enter Bardolph with a cup of sack.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Sir John, there’s one Master Brook below would fain speak with you and

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: be acquainted with you, and hath sent your worship a morning’s draught

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: of sack.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Brook is his name?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Ay, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Call him in.
[_Exit Bardolph._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Such Brooks are welcome to me, that o’erflow such liquor. Ah, ha,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mistress Ford and Mistress Page, have I encompassed you? Go to, _via!_
Enter Bardolph with Ford disguised as Brook.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: God bless you, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: And you, sir. Would you speak with me?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I make bold to press with so little preparation upon you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You’re welcome. What’s your will?—Give us leave, drawer.
[_Exit Bardolph._]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Sir, I am a gentleman that have spent much. My name is Brook.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Good Master Brook, I desire more acquaintance of you.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Good Sir John, I sue for yours; not to charge you, for I must let you

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: understand I think myself in better plight for a lender than you are,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: the which hath something emboldened me to this unseasoned intrusion;

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: for they say, if money go before, all ways do lie open.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Money is a good soldier, sir, and will on.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Troth, and I have a bag of money here troubles me. If you will help to

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: bear it, Sir John, take all, or half, for easing me of the carriage.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Sir, I know not how I may deserve to be your porter.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I will tell you, sir, if you will give me the hearing.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Speak, good Master Brook. I shall be glad to be your servant.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Sir, I hear you are a scholar—I will be brief with you—and you have

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: been a man long known to me, though I had never so good means as desire

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: to make myself acquainted with you. I shall discover a thing to you,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: wherein I must very much lay open mine own imperfection. But, good Sir

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: John, as you have one eye upon my follies, as you hear them unfolded,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: turn another into the register of your own, that I may pass with a

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: reproof the easier, sith you yourself know how easy it is to be such an

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: offender.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Very well, sir, proceed.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: There is a gentlewoman in this town, her husband’s name is Ford.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, sir.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I have long loved her, and, I protest to you, bestowed much on her,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: followed her with a doting observance, engrossed opportunities to meet

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: her, fee’d every slight occasion that could but niggardly give me sight

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: of her, not only bought many presents to give her, but have given

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: largely to many to know what she would have given. Briefly, I have

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: pursued her as love hath pursued me, which hath been on the wing of all

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: occasions. But whatsoever I have merited, either in my mind or in my

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: means, meed, I am sure, I have received none, unless experience be a

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: jewel. That I have purchased at an infinite rate, and that hath taught

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: me to say this:

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Love like a shadow flies when substance love pursues,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Pursuing that that flies, and flying what pursues.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Have you received no promise of satisfaction at her hands?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Never.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Have you importuned her to such a purpose?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Never.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Of what quality was your love, then?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Like a fair house built on another man’s ground, so that I have lost my

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: edifice by mistaking the place where I erected it.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: To what purpose have you unfolded this to me?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: When I have told you that, I have told you all. Some say that though

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: she appear honest to me, yet in other places she enlargeth her mirth so

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: far that there is shrewd construction made of her. Now, Sir John, here

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: is the heart of my purpose: you are a gentleman of excellent breeding,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: admirable discourse, of great admittance, authentic in your place and

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: person, generally allowed for your many warlike, courtlike, and learned

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: preparations.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: O, sir!

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Believe it, for you know it. There is money. Spend it, spend it; spend

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: more; spend all I have; only give me so much of your time in exchange

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: of it as to lay an amiable siege to the honesty of this Ford’s wife.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Use your art of wooing, win her to consent to you. If any man may, you

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: may as soon as any.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Would it apply well to the vehemency of your affection that I should

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: win what you would enjoy? Methinks you prescribe to yourself very

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: preposterously.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: O, understand my drift. She dwells so securely on the excellency of her

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: honour that the folly of my soul dares not present itself; she is too

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: bright to be looked against. Now, could I come to her with any

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: detection in my hand, my desires had instance and argument to commend

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: themselves. I could drive her then from the ward of her purity, her

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: reputation, her marriage vow, and a thousand other her defences, which

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: now are too too strongly embattled against me. What say you to’t, Sir

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: John?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Brook, I will first make bold with your money; next, give me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: your hand; and last, as I am a gentleman, you shall, if you will, enjoy

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ford’s wife.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: O good sir!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I say you shall.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Want no money, Sir John; you shall want none.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Want no Mistress Ford, Master Brook; you shall want none. I shall be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: with her, I may tell you, by her own appointment; even as you came in

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: to me, her assistant or go-between parted from me. I say I shall be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: with her between ten and eleven, for at that time the jealous rascally

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: knave her husband will be forth. Come you to me at night. You shall

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: know how I speed.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I am blessed in your acquaintance. Do you know Ford, sir?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hang him, poor cuckoldly knave! I know him not. Yet I wrong him to call

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: him poor. They say the jealous wittolly knave hath masses of money, for

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the which his wife seems to me well-favoured. I will use her as the key

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of the cuckoldly rogue’s coffer, and there’s my harvest-home.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I would you knew Ford, sir, that you might avoid him if you saw him.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Hang him, mechanical salt-butter rogue! I will stare him out of his

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: wits, I will awe him with my cudgel; it shall hang like a meteor o’er

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the cuckold’s horns. Master Brook, thou shalt know I will predominate

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: over the peasant, and thou shalt lie with his wife. Come to me soon at

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: night. Ford’s a knave, and I will aggravate his style. Thou, Master

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Brook, shalt know him for knave and cuckold. Come to me soon at night.
[_Exit Falstaff._]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: What a damned epicurean rascal is this! My heart is ready to crack with

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: impatience. Who says this is improvident jealousy? My wife hath sent to

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: him, the hour is fixed, the match is made. Would any man have thought

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: this? See the hell of having a false woman: my bed shall be abused, my

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: coffers ransacked, my reputation gnawn at; and I shall not only receive

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: this villanous wrong, but stand under the adoption of abominable terms,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: and by him that does me this wrong. Terms, names! Amaimon sounds well;

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Lucifer, well; Barbason, well; yet they are devils’ additions, the

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: names of fiends. But cuckold? Wittol? Cuckold? The devil himself hath

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: not such a name. Page is an ass, a secure ass; he will trust his wife,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: he will not be jealous. I will rather trust a Fleming with my butter,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Parson Hugh the Welshman with my cheese, an Irishman with my aqua-vitae

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: bottle, or a thief to walk my ambling gelding, than my wife with

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: herself. Then she plots, then she ruminates, then she devises; and what

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: they think in their hearts they may effect, they will break their

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: hearts but they will effect. God be praised for my jealousy! Eleven

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: o’clock the hour. I will prevent this, detect my wife, be revenged on

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Falstaff, and laugh at Page. I will about it. Better three hours too

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: soon than a minute too late. Fie, fie, fie! Cuckold, cuckold, cuckold!
[_Exit._]
Enter Doctor Caius and Rugby.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Jack Rugby!

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: Sir?

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Vat is de clock, Jack?

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: ’Tis past the hour, sir, that Sir Hugh promised to meet.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, he has save his soul, dat he is no come. He has pray his Pible

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: well dat he is no come. By gar, Jack Rugby, he is dead already, if he

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: be come.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: He is wise, sir; he knew your worship would kill him if he came.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, de herring is no dead so as I vill kill him. Take your rapier,

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Jack; I vill tell you how I vill kill him.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: Alas, sir, I cannot fence.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Villainy, take your rapier.

lines.speaker: RUGBY
lines.text: Forbear; here’s company.
Enter Page, Shallow, Slender and Host.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: God bless thee, bully doctor!

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: God save you, Master Doctor Caius!

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Now, good Master Doctor!

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Give you good morrow, sir.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Vat be all you, one, two, tree, four, come for?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: To see thee fight, to see thee foin, to see thee traverse; to see thee

lines.speaker: HOST
