lines.text: here, to see thee there; to see thee pass thy punto, thy stock, thy

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: reverse, thy distance, thy montant. Is he dead, my Ethiopian? Is he

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: dead, my Francisco? Ha, bully? What says my Aesculapius, my Galen, my

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: heart of elder, ha? Is he dead, bully stale? Is he dead?

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, he is de coward Jack-priest of de vorld. He is not show his

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: face.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Thou art a Castalion King Urinal Hector of Greece, my boy!

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: I pray you, bear witness that me have stay six or seven, two, tree

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: hours for him, and he is no come.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: He is the wiser man, Master doctor. He is a curer of souls, and you a

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: curer of bodies. If you should fight, you go against the hair of your

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: professions. Is it not true, Master Page?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Master Shallow, you have yourself been a great fighter, though now a

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: man of peace.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Bodykins, Master Page, though I now be old, and of the peace, if I see

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: a sword out, my finger itches to make one. Though we are justices and

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: doctors and churchmen, Master Page, we have some salt of our youth in

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: us. We are the sons of women, Master Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: ’Tis true, Master Shallow.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: It will be found so, Master Page.—Master Doctor Caius, I come to fetch

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: you home. I am sworn of the peace. You have showed yourself a wise

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: physician, and Sir Hugh hath shown himself a wise and patient

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: churchman. You must go with me, Master Doctor.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Pardon, guest justice.—A word, Monsieur Mockwater.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Mockvater? Vat is dat?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Mockwater, in our English tongue, is valour, bully.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, then I have as much mockvater as de Englishman. Scurvy jack-dog

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: priest! By gar, me vill cut his ears.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: He will clapper-claw thee tightly, bully.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Clapper-de-claw? Vat is dat?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: That is, he will make thee amends.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, me do look he shall clapper-de-claw me, for, by gar, me vill

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: have it.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: And I will provoke him to’t, or let him wag.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Me tank you for dat.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: And, moreover, bully—but first, Master guest, and Master Page, and eke

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Cavaliero Slender, go you through the town to Frogmore.
[_Aside to Host_.]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Sir Hugh is there, is he?
[_Aside to Page_.]

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: He is there. See what humour he is in; and I will

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: bring the doctor about by the fields. Will it do well?
[_Aside to Host_.]

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: We will do it.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: PAGE, SHALLOW and SLENDER

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Adieu, good Master Doctor.
[_Exeunt Page, Shallow and Slender._]

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, me vill kill de priest, for he speak for a jackanape to Anne

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Page.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Let him die. Sheathe thy impatience; throw cold water on thy choler. Go

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: about the fields with me through Frogmore. I will bring thee where

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Mistress Anne Page is, at a farm-house a-feasting, and thou shalt woo

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: her. Cried game! Said I well?

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, me tank you for dat. By gar, I love you; and I shall procure-a

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: you de good guest: de earl, de knight, de lords, de gentlemen, my

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: patients.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: For the which I will be thy adversary toward Anne Page. Said I well?

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, ’tis good; vell said.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Let us wag, then.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Come at my heels, Jack Rugby.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Sir Hugh Evans and Simple.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: I pray you now, good Master Slender’s servingman, and friend Simple by

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: your name, which way have you looked for Master Caius, that calls

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: himself doctor of physic?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Marry, sir, the Petty-ward, the Park-ward, every way; old Windsor way,

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: and every way but the town way.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: I most fehemently desire you, you will also look that way.

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: I will, Sir.
[_Exit Simple._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Pless my soul, how full of cholers I am, and trempling of mind! I shall

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: be glad if he have deceived me. How melancholies I am! I will knog his

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: urinals about his knave’s costard when I have good opportunities for

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: the ’ork. Pless my soul!
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: _To shallow rivers, to whose falls

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Melodious birds sings madrigals.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: There will we make our peds of roses

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: And a thousand fragrant posies.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: To shallow_—

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Mercy on me, I have a great dispositions to cry.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: _Melodious birds sing madrigals—

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Whenas I sat in Pabylon—

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: And a thousand vagram posies.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: To shallow rivers, to whose falls

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Melodious birds sing madrigals._
Enter Simple.

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: Yonder he is, coming this way, Sir Hugh.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: He’s welcome.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: _To shallow rivers, to whose falls—_

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Heaven prosper the right! What weapons is he?

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: No weapons, sir. There comes my master, Master Shallow, and another

lines.speaker: SIMPLE
lines.text: gentleman, from Frogmore, over the stile, this way.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Pray you, give me my gown—or else keep it in your arms.
Enter Page, Shallow and Slender.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: How now, Master Parson? Good morrow, good Sir Hugh. Keep a gamester

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: from the dice, and a good student from his book, and it is wonderful.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ah, sweet Anne Page!

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: God save you, good Sir Hugh!

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: God pless you from his mercy sake, all of you!

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: What, the sword and the word? Do you study them both, Master Parson?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: And youthful still—in your doublet and hose, this raw rheumatic day?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: There is reasons and causes for it.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: We are come to you to do a good office, Master Parson.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Fery well; what is it?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Yonder is a most reverend gentleman who, belike having received wrong

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: by some person, is at most odds with his own gravity and patience that

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: ever you saw.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I have lived fourscore years and upward; I never heard a man of his

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: place, gravity, and learning, so wide of his own respect.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: What is he?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I think you know him: Master Doctor Caius, the renowned French

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: physician.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Got’s will and His passion of my heart! I had as lief you would tell me

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: of a mess of porridge.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: He has no more knowledge in Hibbocrates and Galen, and he is a knave

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: besides, a cowardly knave as you would desires to be acquainted withal.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I warrant you, he’s the man should fight with him.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: O, sweet Anne Page!

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: It appears so by his weapons. Keep them asunder. Here comes Doctor

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Caius.
Enter Host, Caius and Rugby.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Nay, good Master Parson, keep in your weapon.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: So do you, good Master Doctor.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Disarm them, and let them question. Let them keep their limbs whole and

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: hack our English.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: I pray you, let-a me speak a word with your ear. Verefore will you not

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: meet-a me?
[_Aside to Caius_.]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Pray you, use your patience. In good time.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, you are de coward, de Jack dog, John ape.
[_Aside to Caius_.]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Pray you, let us not be laughing stocks to other

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: men’s humours. I desire you in friendship, and I will one way or other

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: make you amends.
[_Aloud_.]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: By Jeshu, I will knog your urinal about your knave’s

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: cogscomb.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: _Diable!_ Jack Rugby, mine Host de Jarteer, have I not stay for him to

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: kill him? Have I not, at de place I did appoint?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: As I am a Christians soul, now look you, this is the place appointed.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: I’ll be judgment by mine host of the Garter.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Peace, I say, Gallia and Gaul, French and Welsh, soul-curer and

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: body-curer!

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Ay, dat is very good; excellent.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Peace, I say! Hear mine host of the Garter. Am I politic? Am I subtle?

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Am I a Machiavel? Shall I lose my doctor? No, he gives me the potions

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: and the motions. Shall I lose my parson, my priest, my Sir Hugh? No, he

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: gives me the proverbs and the no-verbs. [_To Caius_.] Give me thy hand,

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: terrestrial; so. [_To Evans_.] Give me thy hand, celestial; so. Boys of

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: art, I have deceived you both. I have directed you to wrong places.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Your hearts are mighty, your skins are whole, and let burnt sack be the

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: issue. Come, lay their swords to pawn. Follow me, lads of peace,

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: follow, follow, follow.
[_Exit Host._]

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Afore God, a mad host! Follow, gentlemen, follow.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: O, sweet Anne Page!
[_Exeunt Shallow, Slender and Page._]

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Ha, do I perceive dat? Have you make-a de sot of us, ha, ha?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: This is well, he has made us his vlouting-stog. I desire you that we

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: may be friends, and let us knog our prains together to be revenge on

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: this same scall, scurvy, cogging companion, the host of the Garter.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, with all my heart. He promise to bring me where is Anne Page;

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: by gar, he deceive me too.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Well, I will smite his noddles. Pray you follow.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Mistress Page following Robin.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Nay, keep your way, little gallant. You were wont to be a follower, but

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: now you are a leader. Whether had you rather, lead mine eyes, or eye

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: your master’s heels?

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: I had rather, forsooth, go before you like a man than follow him like a

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: dwarf.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: O, you are a flattering boy! Now I see you’ll be a courtier.
Enter Ford.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Well met, Mistress Page. Whither go you?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Truly, sir, to see your wife. Is she at home?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Ay, and as idle as she may hang together, for want of company. I think

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: if your husbands were dead you two would marry.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Be sure of that—two other husbands.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Where had you this pretty weathercock?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I cannot tell what the dickens his name is my husband had him of. What

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: do you call your knight’s name, sirrah?

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: Sir John Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Sir John Falstaff!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: He, he; I can never hit on’s name. There is such a league between my

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: good man and he! Is your wife at home indeed?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Indeed she is.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: By your leave, sir, I am sick till I see her.
[_Exeunt Mistress Page and Robin._]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Has Page any brains? Hath he any eyes? Hath he any thinking? Sure, they

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: sleep; he hath no use of them. Why, this boy will carry a letter twenty

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: mile as easy as a cannon will shoot point-blank twelve score. He pieces

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: out his wife’s inclination, he gives her folly motion and advantage.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: And now she’s going to my wife, and Falstaff’s boy with her. A man may

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: hear this shower sing in the wind. And Falstaff’s boy with her! Good

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: plots they are laid, and our revolted wives share damnation together.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Well, I will take him, then torture my wife, pluck the borrowed veil of

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: modesty from the so-seeming Mistress Page, divulge Page himself for a

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: secure and wilful Actaeon, and to these violent proceedings all my

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: neighbours shall cry aim. [_Clock strikes_.] The clock gives me my cue,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: and my assurance bids me search. There I shall find Falstaff. I shall

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: be rather praised for this than mocked, for it is as positive as the

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: earth is firm that Falstaff is there. I will go.
Enter Page, Shallow, Slender, Host, Sir Hugh Evans, Caius and Rugby.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: SHALLOW, PAGE, etc.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Well met, Master Ford.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Trust me, a good knot. I have good cheer at home, and I pray you all go

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: with me.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: I must excuse myself, Master Ford.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: And so must I, sir; we have appointed to dine with Mistress Anne, and I

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: would not break with her for more money than I’ll speak of.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: We have lingered about a match between Anne Page and my cousin Slender,

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: and this day we shall have our answer.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I hope I have your good will, father Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: You have, Master Slender, I stand wholly for you.—But my wife, Master

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: doctor, is for you altogether.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Ay, be-gar; and de maid is love-a me! My nursh-a Quickly tell me so

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: mush.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: What say you to young Master Fenton? He capers, he dances, he has eyes

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: of youth, he writes verses, he speaks holiday, he smells April and May.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: He will carry ’t, he will carry ’t. ’Tis in his buttons he will carry

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Not by my consent, I promise you. The gentleman is of no having. He

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: kept company with the wild Prince and Poins. He is of too high a

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: region, he knows too much. No, he shall not knit a knot in his fortunes

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: with the finger of my substance. If he take her, let him take her

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: simply. The wealth I have waits on my consent, and my consent goes not

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: that way.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I beseech you, heartily, some of you go home with me to dinner. Besides

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: your cheer, you shall have sport: I will show you a monster. Master

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Doctor, you shall go; so shall you, Master Page, and you, Sir Hugh.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Well, fare you well. We shall have the freer wooing at Master Page’s.
[_Exeunt Shallow and Slender._]

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Go home, John Rugby; I come anon.
[_Exit Rugby._]

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: Farewell, my hearts. I will to my honest knight Falstaff, and drink

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: canary with him.
[_Exit Host._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I think I shall drink in pipe-wine first with him; I’ll make

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: him dance.—Will you go, gentles?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Have with you to see this monster.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Mistress Ford and Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What, John! What, Robert!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Quickly, quickly! Is the buck-basket—

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I warrant.—What, Robin, I say!
Enter John and Robert with a great buck-basket.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Come, come, come.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Here, set it down.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Give your men the charge; we must be brief.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Marry, as I told you before, John and Robert, be ready here hard by in

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: the brew-house; and when I suddenly call you, come forth, and, without

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: any pause or staggering, take this basket on your shoulders. That done,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: trudge with it in all haste, and carry it among the whitsters in

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Datchet Mead, and there empty it in the muddy ditch close by the Thames

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: side.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: You will do it?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I ha’ told them over and over, they lack no direction.—Be gone, and

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: come when you are called.
[_Exeunt John and Robert._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Here comes little Robin.
Enter Robin.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: How now, my eyas-musket, what news with you?

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: My Master, Sir John, is come in at your back door, Mistress Ford, and

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: requests your company.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: You little Jack-a-Lent, have you been true to us?

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: Ay, I’ll be sworn. My master knows not of your being here, and hath

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: threatened to put me into everlasting liberty if I tell you of it; for

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: he swears he’ll turn me away.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Thou’rt a good boy, this secrecy of thine shall be a tailor to thee,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: and shall make thee a new doublet and hose. I’ll go hide me.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Do so.—Go tell thy master I am alone.
[_Exit Robin._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Mistress Page, remember you your cue.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I warrant thee. If I do not act it, hiss me.
[_Exit Mistress Page._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Go to, then. We’ll use this unwholesome humidity, this gross watery

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: pumpion; we’ll teach him to know turtles from jays.
Enter Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: “Have I caught thee, my heavenly jewel?” Why, now let me die, for I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have lived long enough. This is the period of my ambition. O this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: blessed hour!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: O, sweet Sir John!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mistress Ford, I cannot cog, I cannot prate, Mistress Ford. Now shall I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: sin in my wish: I would thy husband were dead. I’ll speak it before the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: best lord: I would make thee my lady.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I your lady, Sir John? Alas, I should be a pitiful lady.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let the court of France show me such another. I see how thine eye would

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: emulate the diamond. Thou hast the right arched beauty of the brow that

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: becomes the ship-tire, the tire-valiant, or any tire of Venetian

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: admittance.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: A plain kerchief, Sir John. My brows become nothing else, nor that well

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: neither.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: By the Lord, thou art a traitor to say so. Thou wouldst make an

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: absolute courtier, and the firm fixture of thy foot would give an

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: excellent motion to thy gait in a semi-circled farthingale. I see what

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: thou wert, if Fortune thy foe were not, Nature thy friend. Come, thou

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: canst not hide it.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Believe me, there’s no such thing in me.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What made me love thee? Let that persuade thee there’s something

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: extraordinary in thee. Come, I cannot cog and say thou art this and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: that, like a many of these lisping hawthorn buds that come like women

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: in men’s apparel, and smell like Bucklersbury in simple-time. I cannot.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: But I love thee, none but thee; and thou deservest it.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Do not betray me, sir; I fear you love Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Thou mightst as well say I love to walk by the Counter gate, which is

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: as hateful to me as the reek of a lime-kiln.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Well, heaven knows how I love you, and you shall one day find it.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Keep in that mind, I’ll deserve it.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Nay, I must tell you, so you do; or else I could not be in that mind.
Enter Robin.

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: Mistress Ford, Mistress Ford, here’s Mistress Page at the door,

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: sweating and blowing and looking wildly, and would needs speak with you

lines.speaker: ROBIN
lines.text: presently.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: She shall not see me; I will ensconce me behind the arras.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Pray you, do so; she’s a very tattling woman.
[_Falstaff hides himself behind the arras._]
Enter Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What’s the matter? How now?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: O Mistress Ford, what have you done? You’re shamed, you’re overthrown,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: you’re undone for ever!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What’s the matter, good Mistress Page?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: O well-a-day, Mistress Ford, having an honest man to your husband, to

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: give him such cause of suspicion!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What cause of suspicion?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What cause of suspicion? Out upon you! How am I mistook in you!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, alas, what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Your husband’s coming hither, woman, with all the officers in Windsor,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: to search for a gentleman that he says is here now in the house, by

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: your consent, to take an ill advantage of his absence. You are undone.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: ’Tis not so, I hope.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Pray heaven it be not so, that you have such a man here! But ’tis most

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: certain your husband’s coming, with half Windsor at his heels, to

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: search for such a one. I come before to tell you. If you know yourself

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: clear, why, I am glad of it; but if you have a friend here, convey,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: convey him out. Be not amazed, call all your senses to you; defend your

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: reputation, or bid farewell to your good life for ever.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What shall I do? There is a gentleman, my dear friend; and I fear not

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: mine own shame as much as his peril. I had rather than a thousand pound

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: he were out of the house.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: For shame! Never stand “you had rather” and “you had rather”. Your

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: husband’s here at hand. Bethink you of some conveyance. In the house

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: you cannot hide him. O, how have you deceived me! Look, here is a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: basket. If he be of any reasonable stature, he may creep in here; and

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: throw foul linen upon him, as if it were going to bucking. Or—it is

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: whiting-time—send him by your two men to Datchet Mead.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: He’s too big to go in there. What shall I do?
[_Comes out of hiding_.]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let me see ’t, let me see ’t! O, let me see

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ’t! I’ll in, I’ll in. Follow your friend’s counsel. I’ll in.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What, Sir John Falstaff? Are these your letters, knight?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I love thee, and none but thee. Help me away. Let me creep in here.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I’ll never—
[_He goes into the basket; they cover him with dirty clothes._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Help to cover your master, boy.—Call your men, Mistress Ford.—You

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: dissembling knight!
[_Exit Robin._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What, John! Robert! John!
Enter John and Robert.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Go, take up these clothes here, quickly. Where’s the cowl-staff? Look

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: how you drumble! Carry them to the laundress in Datchet Mead; quickly,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: come.
Enter Ford, Page, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Pray you come near. If I suspect without cause, why then make sport at

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: me, then let me be your jest; I deserve it.—How now? Whither bear you

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: this?

lines.speaker: JOHN and ROBERT
lines.text: To the laundress, forsooth.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, what have you to do whither they bear it? You were best meddle

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: with buck-washing!

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Buck? I would I could wash myself of the buck! Buck, buck, buck! Ay,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: buck! I warrant you, buck, and of the season too, it shall appear.
[_Exeunt John and Robert with the basket._]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Gentlemen, I have dreamed tonight; I’ll tell you my dream. Here, here,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: here be my keys. Ascend my chambers, search, seek, find out. I’ll

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: warrant we’ll unkennel the fox. Let me stop this way first. [_Locks the

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: door_.] So, now uncape.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Good Master Ford, be contented: you wrong yourself too much.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: True, Master Page.—Up, gentlemen, you shall see sport anon. Follow me,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: gentlemen.
[_Exit Ford._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: This is fery fantastical humours and jealousies.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, ’tis no the fashion of France; it is not jealous in France.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Nay, follow him, gentlemen; see the issue of his search.
[_Exeunt Page, Evans and Caius._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Is there not a double excellency in this?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I know not which pleases me better, that my husband is deceived, or Sir

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: John.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What a taking was he in when your husband asked who was in the basket!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I am half afraid he will have need of washing, so throwing him into the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: water will do him a benefit.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Hang him, dishonest rascal! I would all of the same strain were in the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: same distress.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I think my husband hath some special suspicion of Falstaff’s being

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: here, for I never saw him so gross in his jealousy till now.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I will lay a plot to try that, and we will yet have more tricks with

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Falstaff. His dissolute disease will scarce obey this medicine.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Shall we send that foolish carrion Mistress Quickly to him, and excuse

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: his throwing into the water, and give him another hope, to betray him

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: to another punishment?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: We will do it. Let him be sent for tomorrow eight o’clock to have

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: amends.
Enter Ford, Page, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I cannot find him. Maybe the knave bragged of that he could not

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: compass.
[_Aside to Mistress Ford_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Heard you that?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: You use me well, Master Ford, do you?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Ay, I do so.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Heaven make you better than your thoughts!

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Amen!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: You do yourself mighty wrong, Master Ford.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Ay, ay; I must bear it.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: If there be anypody in the house, and in the chambers, and in the

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: coffers, and in the presses, heaven forgive my sins at the day of

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: judgment!

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Be gar, nor I too; there is nobodies.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Fie, fie, Master Ford, are you not ashamed? What spirit, what devil

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: suggests this imagination? I would not ha’ your distemper in this kind

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: for the wealth of Windsor Castle.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: ’Tis my fault, Master Page. I suffer for it.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: You suffer for a pad conscience. Your wife is as honest a ’omans as I

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: will desires among five thousand, and five hundred too.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: By gar, I see ’tis an honest woman.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Well, I promised you a dinner. Come, come, walk in the park. I pray you

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: pardon me; I will hereafter make known to you why I have done this.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Come, wife, come, Mistress Page, I pray you pardon me. Pray heartily,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: pardon me.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Let’s go in, gentlemen; but, trust me, we’ll mock him. I do invite you

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: tomorrow morning to my house to breakfast; after, we’ll a-birding

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: together; I have a fine hawk for the bush. Shall it be so?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Anything.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: If there is one, I shall make two in the company.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: If there be one or two, I shall make-a the turd.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Pray you go, Master Page.
[_Exeunt all but Evans and Caius._]

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: I pray you now, remembrance tomorrow on the lousy knave, mine host.

lines.speaker: CAIUS
lines.text: Dat is good, by gar, with all my heart.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: A lousy knave, to have his gibes and his mockeries!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Fenton and Anne Page.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: I see I cannot get thy father’s love;

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Therefore no more turn me to him, sweet Nan.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Alas, how then?

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Why, thou must be thyself.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: He doth object I am too great of birth,

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: And that my state being galled with my expense,

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: I seek to heal it only by his wealth.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Besides these, other bars he lays before me:

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: My riots past, my wild societies—

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: And tells me ’tis a thing impossible

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: I should love thee but as a property.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Maybe he tells you true.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: No, heaven so speed me in my time to come!

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Albeit I will confess thy father’s wealth

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Was the first motive that I wooed thee, Anne,

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Yet, wooing thee, I found thee of more value

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Than stamps in gold or sums in sealed bags.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: And ’tis the very riches of thyself

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: That now I aim at.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Gentle Master Fenton,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Yet seek my father’s love, still seek it, sir.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: If opportunity and humblest suit

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Cannot attain it, why then—hark you hither.
[_They talk apart._]
Enter Shallow, Slender and Mistress Quickly.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Break their talk, Mistress Quickly. My kinsman shall speak for himself.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I’ll make a shaft or a bolt on ’t. ’Slid, ’tis but venturing.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Be not dismayed.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: No, she shall not dismay me. I care not for that, but that I am afeard.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Hark ye, Master Slender would speak a word with you.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I come to him.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: This is my father’s choice.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: O, what a world of vile ill-favoured faults

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Looks handsome in three hundred pounds a year!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: And how does good Master Fenton? Pray you, a word with you.
[_They talk aside._]
[_To Slender_.]

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: She’s coming; to her, coz. O boy, thou hadst a father!

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: I had a father, Mistress Anne; my uncle can tell you good jests of

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: him.—Pray you, uncle, tell Mistress Anne the jest how my father stole

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: two geese out of a pen, good uncle.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Mistress Anne, my cousin loves you.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, that I do, as well as I love any woman in Gloucestershire.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: He will maintain you like a gentlewoman.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Ay, that I will, come cut and long-tail, under the degree of a squire.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: He will make you a hundred and fifty pounds jointure.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Good Master Shallow, let him woo for himself.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Marry, I thank you for it, I thank you for that good comfort.—She calls

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: you, coz; I’ll leave you.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Now, Master Slender.

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Now, good Mistress Anne.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: What is your will?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: My will? ’Od’s heartlings, that’s a pretty jest indeed! I ne’er made my

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: will yet, I thank heaven. I am not such a sickly creature, I give

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: heaven praise.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: I mean, Master Slender, what would you with me?

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: Truly, for mine own part I would little or nothing with you. Your

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: father and my uncle hath made motions. If it be my luck, so; if not,

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: happy man be his dole. They can tell you how things go better than I

lines.speaker: SLENDER
lines.text: can. You may ask your father. Here he comes.
Enter Page and Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Now, Master Slender.—Love him, daughter Anne.—

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Why, how now? What does Master Fenton here?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: You wrong me, sir, thus still to haunt my house.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: I told you, sir, my daughter is disposed of.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Nay, Master Page, be not impatient.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Good Master Fenton, come not to my child.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: She is no match for you.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Sir, will you hear me?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: No, good Master Fenton.—

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Come, Master Shallow; come, son Slender, in.—

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Knowing my mind, you wrong me, Master Fenton.
[_Exeunt Page, Shallow and Slender._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Speak to Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Good Mistress Page, for that I love your daughter

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: In such a righteous fashion as I do,

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Perforce, against all checks, rebukes, and manners,

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: I must advance the colours of my love

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: And not retire. Let me have your good will.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Good mother, do not marry me to yond fool.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I mean it not; I seek you a better husband.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: That’s my master, Master Doctor.

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: Alas, I had rather be set quick i’ th’ earth,

lines.speaker: ANNE
lines.text: And bowled to death with turnips.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Come, trouble not yourself, good Master Fenton,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I will not be your friend, nor enemy.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: My daughter will I question how she loves you,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And as I find her, so am I affected.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Till then, farewell, sir. She must needs go in;

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Her father will be angry.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Farewell, gentle mistress. Farewell, Nan.
[_Exeunt Mistress Page and Anne._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: This is my doing now. “Nay,” said I, “will you cast away your child on

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: a fool, and a physician? Look on Master Fenton.” This is my doing.

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: I thank thee; and I pray thee, once tonight

lines.speaker: FENTON
lines.text: Give my sweet Nan this ring. There’s for thy pains.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Now Heaven send thee good fortune!
[_Exit Fenton._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: A kind heart he hath. A woman would run through fire and water for such

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: a kind heart. But yet I would my master had Mistress Anne, or I would

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Master Slender had her; or, in sooth, I would Master Fenton had her. I

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: will do what I can for them all three, for so I have promised and I’ll

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: be as good as my word—but speciously for Master Fenton. Well, I must of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: another errand to Sir John Falstaff from my two mistresses. What a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: beast am I to slack it!
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: A room in the Garter Inn

lines.text: Enter Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Bardolph, I say!
Enter Bardolph.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Here, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Go fetch me a quart of sack; put a toast in ’t.
[_Exit Bardolph._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Have I lived to be carried in a basket like a barrow of butcher’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: offal, and to be thrown in the Thames? Well, if I be served such

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: another trick, I’ll have my brains ta’en out and buttered, and give

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: them to a dog for a New Year’s gift. ’Sblood, the rogues slighted me

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: into the river with as little remorse as they would have drowned a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: blind bitch’s puppies, fifteen i’ the litter; and you may know by my

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: size that I have a kind of alacrity in sinking; if the bottom were as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: deep as hell, I should down. I had been drowned, but that the shore was

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shelvy and shallow—a death that I abhor, for the water swells a man,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and what a thing should I have been when I had been swelled! I should

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have been a mountain of mummy.
Enter Bardolph with sack.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Here’s Mistress Quickly, sir, to speak with you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Come, let me pour in some sack to the Thames water, for my belly’s as

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: cold as if I had swallowed snowballs for pills to cool the reins. Call

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: her in.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Come in, woman.
Enter Mistress Quickly.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: By your leave, I cry you mercy. Give your worship good morrow.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Take away these chalices. Go, brew me a pottle of sack finely.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: With eggs, sir?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Simple of itself. I’ll no pullet sperm in my brewage.
[_Exit Bardolph._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: How now?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Marry, sir, I come to your worship from Mistress Ford.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mistress Ford? I have had ford enough. I was thrown into the ford, I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: have my belly full of ford.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Alas the day, good heart, that was not her fault. She does so take on

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: with her men; they mistook their erection.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: So did I mine, to build upon a foolish woman’s promise.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Well, she laments, sir, for it, that it would yearn your heart to see

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: it. Her husband goes this morning a-birding; she desires you once more

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: to come to her, between eight and nine. I must carry her word quickly.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: She’ll make you amends, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, I will visit her. Tell her so, and bid her think what a man is.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Let her consider his frailty, and then judge of my merit.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: I will tell her.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Do so. Between nine and ten, sayst thou?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Eight and nine, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Well, be gone. I will not miss her.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Peace be with you, sir.
[_Exit Mistress Quickly._]

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I marvel I hear not of Master Brook; he sent me word to stay within. I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: like his money well. O, here he comes.
Enter Ford disguised.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: God bless you, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Now, Master Brook, you come to know what hath passed between me and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Ford’s wife?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: That indeed, Sir John, is my business.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Brook, I will not lie to you. I was at her house the hour she

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: appointed me.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: And how sped you, sir?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Very ill-favouredly, Master Brook.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: How so, sir? Did she change her determination?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No. Master Brook, but the peaking cornuto her husband, Master Brook,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: dwelling in a continual ’larum of jealousy, comes me in the instant of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: our encounter, after we had embraced, kissed, protested, and, as it

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: were, spoke the prologue of our comedy; and at his heels a rabble of

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: his companions, thither provoked and instigated by his distemper, and,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: forsooth, to search his house for his wife’s love.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: What, while you were there?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: While I was there.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: And did he search for you, and could not find you?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: You shall hear. As good luck would have it, comes in one Mistress Page,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: gives intelligence of Ford’s approach; and, in her invention and Ford’s

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: wife’s distraction, they conveyed me into a buck-basket.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: A buck-basket!

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: By the Lord, a buck-basket! Rammed me in with foul shirts and smocks,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: socks, foul stockings, greasy napkins, that, Master Brook, there was

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: the rankest compound of villainous smell that ever offended nostril.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: And how long lay you there?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Nay, you shall hear, Master Brook, what I have suffered to bring this

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: woman to evil for your good. Being thus crammed in the basket, a couple

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: of Ford’s knaves, his hinds, were called forth by their mistress to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: carry me in the name of foul clothes to Datchet Lane. They took me on

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: their shoulders, met the jealous knave their master in the door, who

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: asked them once or twice what they had in their basket. I quaked for

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fear lest the lunatic knave would have searched it; but Fate, ordaining

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: he should be a cuckold, held his hand. Well, on went he for a search,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: and away went I for foul clothes. But mark the sequel, Master Brook. I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: suffered the pangs of three several deaths: first, an intolerable

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: fright to be detected with a jealous rotten bell-wether; next, to be

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: compassed like a good bilbo in the circumference of a peck, hilt to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: point, heel to head; and then, to be stopped in, like a strong

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: distillation, with stinking clothes that fretted in their own grease.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Think of that, a man of my kidney, think of that—that am as subject to

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: heat as butter; a man of continual dissolution and thaw. It was a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: miracle to ’scape suffocation. And in the height of this bath, when I

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: was more than half stewed in grease, like a Dutch dish, to be thrown

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: into the Thames and cooled, glowing hot, in that surge, like a

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: horseshoe! Think of that—hissing hot—think of that, Master Brook.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: In good sadness, sir, I am sorry that for my sake you have suffered all

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: this. My suit, then, is desperate. You’ll undertake her no more?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Brook, I will be thrown into Etna, as I have been into Thames,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: ere I will leave her thus. Her husband is this morning gone a-birding;

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I have received from her another embassy of meeting. ’Twixt eight and

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: nine is the hour, Master Brook.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: ’Tis past eight already, sir.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Is it? I will then address me to my appointment. Come to me at your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: convenient leisure, and you shall know how I speed; and the conclusion

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: shall be crowned with your enjoying her. Adieu. You shall have her,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Master Brook. Master Brook, you shall cuckold Ford.
[_Exit Falstaff._]

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Hum! Ha! Is this a vision? Is this a dream? Do I sleep? Master Ford,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: awake; awake, Master Ford! There’s a hole made in your best coat,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Master Ford. This ’tis to be married; this ’tis to have linen and

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: buck-baskets! Well, I will proclaim myself what I am. I will now take

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: the lecher. He is at my house. He cannot scape me. ’Tis impossible he

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: should. He cannot creep into a half-penny purse, nor into a pepperbox.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: But, lest the devil that guides him should aid him, I will search

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: impossible places. Though what I am I cannot avoid, yet to be what I

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: would not shall not make me tame. If I have horns to make one mad, let

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: the proverb go with me: I’ll be horn-mad.
[_Exit._]
Enter Mistress Page, Mistress Quickly and William.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Is he at Master Ford’s already, think’st thou?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Sure he is by this; or will be presently. But truly he is very

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: courageous mad about his throwing into the water. Mistress Ford desires

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: you to come suddenly.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I’ll be with her by and by. I’ll but bring my young man here to school.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Look where his master comes; ’tis a playing day, I see.
Enter Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: How now, Sir Hugh, no school today?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: No, Master Slender is let the boys leave to play.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Blessing of his heart!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Sir Hugh, my husband says my son profits nothing in the world at his

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: book. I pray you ask him some questions in his accidence.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Come hither, William. Hold up your head, come.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Come on, sirrah. Hold up your head. Answer your master, be not afraid.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: William, how many numbers is in nouns?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Two.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Truly, I thought there had been one number more, because they say

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: “’Od’s nouns.”

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Peace your tattlings! What is “fair,” William?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: _Pulcher_.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Polecats? There are fairer things than polecats, sure.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: You are a very simplicity ’oman; I pray you, peace.—What is _lapis_,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: William?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: A stone.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: And what is “a stone,” William?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: A pebble.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: No, it is _lapis_. I pray you remember in your prain.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: _Lapis_.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: That is a good William. What is he, William, that does lend articles?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Articles are borrowed of the pronoun, and be thus declined:

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: _singulariter, nominativo, hic, haec, hoc_.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: _Nominativo, hig, haeg, hog_, pray you, mark: _genitivo, huius_. Well,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: what is your accusative case?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: _Accusativo, hinc_.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: I pray you, have your remembrance, child. _Accusativo, hung, hang,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: hog_.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: “Hang-hog” is Latin for bacon, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Leave your prabbles, ’oman.—What is the focative case, William?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: O—_vocativo_—O—

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Remember, William; focative is _caret_.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: And that’s a good root.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: ’Oman, forbear.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Peace.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: What is your genitive case plural, William?

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Genitive case?

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Genitive: _horum, harum, horum_.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: Vengeance of Jenny’s case, fie on her! Never name her, child, if she be

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: a whore.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: For shame, ’oman.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: You do ill to teach the child such words.—He teaches him to hick and to

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: hack, which they’ll do fast enough of themselves; and to call “whore

lines.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
lines.text: ’m”!—Fie upon you!

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: ’Oman, art thou lunatics? Hast thou no understandings for thy cases,

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: and the numbers of the genders? Thou art as foolish Christian creatures

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: as I would desires.
[_To Quickly_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Prithee, hold thy peace.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Show me now, William, some declensions of your pronouns.

lines.speaker: WILLIAM
lines.text: Forsooth, I have forgot.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: It is _qui, quae, quod_. If you forget your _quis_, your _quaes_, and

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: your _quods_, you must be preeches. Go your ways and play, go.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: He is a better scholar than I thought he was.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: He is a good sprag memory. Farewell, Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Adieu, good Sir Hugh.
[_Exit Sir Hugh Evans._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Get you home, boy. Come, we stay too long.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Falstaff and Mistress Ford.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Mistress Ford, your sorrow hath eaten up my sufferance. I see you are

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: obsequious in your love, and I profess requital to a hair’s breadth,

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: not only, Mistress Ford, in the simple office of love, but in all the

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: accoutrement, compliment, and ceremony of it. But are you sure of your

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: husband now?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: He’s a-birding, sweet Sir John.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: What ho, gossip Ford, what ho!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Step into the chamber, Sir John.
[_Exit Falstaff._]
Enter Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: How now, sweetheart, who’s at home besides yourself?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, none but mine own people.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Indeed?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: No, certainly.
[_Aside to her_.]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Speak louder.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Truly, I am so glad you have nobody here.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Why, woman, your husband is in his old lunes again. He so takes on

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: yonder with my husband, so rails against all married mankind, so curses

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: all Eve’s daughters, of what complexion soever, and so buffets himself

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: on the forehead, crying “Peer out, peer out!” that any madness I ever

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: yet beheld seemed but tameness, civility, and patience, to this his

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: distemper he is in now. I am glad the fat knight is not here.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, does he talk of him?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Of none but him, and swears he was carried out, the last time he

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: searched for him, in a basket; protests to my husband he is now here;

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: and hath drawn him and the rest of their company from their sport, to

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: make another experiment of his suspicion. But I am glad the knight is

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: not here. Now he shall see his own foolery.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: How near is he, Mistress Page?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Hard by, at street end. He will be here anon.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I am undone! The knight is here.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Why, then, you are utterly shamed, and he’s but a dead man. What a

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: woman are you! Away with him, away with him! Better shame than murder.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Which way should he go? How should I bestow him? Shall I put him into

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: the basket again?
Enter Falstaff.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: No, I’ll come no more i’ the basket. May I not go out ere he come?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Alas, three of Master Ford’s brothers watch the door with pistols, that

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: none shall issue out, otherwise you might slip away ere he came. But

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: what make you here?

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: What shall I do? I’ll creep up into the chimney.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: There they always use to discharge their birding-pieces.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Creep into the kiln-hole.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Where is it?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: He will seek there, on my word. Neither press, coffer, chest, trunk,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: well, vault, but he hath an abstract for the remembrance of such

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: places, and goes to them by his note. There is no hiding you in the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: house.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: I’ll go out then.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: If you go out in your own semblance, you die, Sir John—unless you go

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: out disguised.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: How might we disguise him?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Alas the day, I know not. There is no woman’s gown big enough for him;

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: otherwise he might put on a hat, a muffler, and a kerchief, and so

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: escape.

lines.speaker: FALSTAFF
lines.text: Good hearts, devise something. Any extremity rather than a mischief.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: My maid’s aunt, the fat woman of Brentford, has a gown above.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: On my word, it will serve him. She’s as big as he is. And there’s her

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: thrummed hat, and her muffler too.—Run up, Sir John.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Go, go, sweet Sir John. Mistress Page and I will look some linen for

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: your head.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Quick, quick! We’ll come dress you straight; put on the gown the while.
[_Exit Falstaff._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I would my husband would meet him in this shape. He cannot abide the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: old woman of Brentford; he swears she’s a witch, forbade her my house,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: and hath threatened to beat her.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Heaven guide him to thy husband’s cudgel and the devil guide his cudgel

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: afterwards!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: But is my husband coming?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Ay, in good sadness is he, and talks of the basket too, howsoever he

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: hath had intelligence.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: We’ll try that; for I’ll appoint my men to carry the basket again, to

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: meet him at the door with it as they did last time.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Nay, but he’ll be here presently. Let’s go dress him like the witch of

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Brentford.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I’ll first direct my men what they shall do with the basket. Go up,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I’ll bring linen for him straight.
[_Exit Mistress Ford._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Hang him, dishonest varlet! We cannot misuse him enough.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: We’ll leave a proof, by that which we will do,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Wives may be merry and yet honest too.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: We do not act that often jest and laugh;

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: ’Tis old but true: “Still swine eats all the draff.”
[_Exit._]
Enter Mistress Ford with John and Robert.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Go, sirs, take the basket again on your shoulders. Your master is hard

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: at door; if he bid you set it down, obey him. Quickly, dispatch.
[_Exit Mistress Ford._]

lines.speaker: JOHN
lines.text: Come, come, take it up.

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Pray heaven it be not full of knight again.

lines.speaker: JOHN
lines.text: I hope not, I had lief as bear so much lead.
Enter Ford, Page, Shallow, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Ay, but if it prove true, Master Page, have you any way then to unfool

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: me again?—Set down the basket, villain! Somebody call my wife. Youth in

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: a basket! O you panderly rascals! There’s a knot, a gin, a pack, a

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: conspiracy against me. Now shall the devil be shamed.—What, wife, I

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: say! Come, come forth! Behold what honest clothes you send forth to

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: bleaching!

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Why, this passes, Master Ford! You are not to go loose any longer; you

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: must be pinioned.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Why, this is lunatics, this is mad as a mad dog.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: Indeed, Master Ford, this is not well, indeed.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: So say I too, sir.
Enter Mistress Ford.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Come hither, Mistress Ford—Mistress Ford, the honest woman, the modest

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: wife, the virtuous creature, that hath the jealous fool to her husband!

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I suspect without cause, mistress, do I?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Heaven be my witness you do, if you suspect me in any dishonesty.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Well said, brazen-face, hold it out.—Come forth, sirrah.
[_Pulls clothes out of the basket._]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: This passes.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Are you not ashamed? Let the clothes alone.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I shall find you anon.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: ’Tis unreasonable. Will you take up your wife’s clothes? Come, away.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Empty the basket, I say.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, man, why?

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Master Page, as I am a man, there was one conveyed out of my house

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: yesterday in this basket. Why may not he be there again? In my house I

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: am sure he is. My intelligence is true, my jealousy is

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: reasonable.—Pluck me out all the linen.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: If you find a man there, he shall die a flea’s death.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Here’s no man.

lines.speaker: SHALLOW
lines.text: By my fidelity, this is not well, Master Ford, this wrongs you.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: Master Ford, you must pray, and not follow the imaginations of your own

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: heart. This is jealousies.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Well, he’s not here I seek for.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: No, nor nowhere else but in your brain.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Help to search my house this one time. If I find not what I seek, show

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: no colour for my extremity, let me for ever be your table-sport. Let

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: them say of me “As jealous as Ford, that searched a hollow walnut for

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: his wife’s leman.” Satisfy me once more, once more search with me.
[_Exeunt John and Robert with the basket._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What, ho, Mistress Page! Come you and the old woman down; my husband

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: will come into the chamber.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Old woman? What old woman’s that?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Why, it is my maid’s aunt of Brentford.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: A witch, a quean, an old cozening quean! Have I not forbid her my

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: house? She comes of errands, does she? We are simple men; we do not

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: know what’s brought to pass under the profession of fortune-telling.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: She works by charms, by spells, by the figure, and such daubery as this

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: is, beyond our element. We know nothing.—Come down, you witch, you hag,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: you! Come down, I say!

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Nay, good sweet husband!—Good gentlemen, let him not strike the old

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: woman.
Enter Falstaff disguised as an old woman, led by Mistress Page.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Come, Mother Prat; come, give me your hand.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I’ll prat her. [_Beats him_.] Out of my door, you witch, you rag, you

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: baggage, you polecat, you runnion! Out, out! I’ll conjure you, I’ll

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: fortune-tell you.
[_Exit Falstaff._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Are you not ashamed? I think you have killed the poor woman.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Nay, he will do it. ’Tis a goodly credit for you.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Hang her, witch!

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: By yea and no, I think the ’oman is a witch indeed. I like not when a

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: ’oman has a great peard. I spy a great peard under her muffler.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Will you follow, gentlemen? I beseech you follow, see but the issue of

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: my jealousy. If I cry out thus upon no trail, never trust me when I

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: open again.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Let’s obey his humour a little further. Come, gentlemen.
[_Exeunt Ford, Page, Caius, Evans and Shallow._]

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Trust me, he beat him most pitifully.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Nay, by th’ mass, that he did not; he beat him most unpitifully,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: methought.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: I’ll have the cudgel hallowed and hung o’er the altar. It hath done

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: meritorious service.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: What think you? May we, with the warrant of womanhood and the witness

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: of a good conscience, pursue him with any further revenge?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: The spirit of wantonness is sure scared out of him. If the devil have

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: him not in fee-simple, with fine and recovery, he will never, I think,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: in the way of waste, attempt us again.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Shall we tell our husbands how we have served him?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Yes, by all means, if it be but to scrape the figures out of your

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: husband’s brains. If they can find in their hearts the poor unvirtuous

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: fat knight shall be any further afflicted, we two will still be the

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: ministers.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: I’ll warrant they’ll have him publicly shamed, and methinks there would

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: be no period to the jest should he not be publicly shamed.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Come, to the forge with it, then shape it. I would not have things

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: cool.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A room in the Garter Inn

lines.text: Enter Host and Bardolph.

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Sir, the Germans desire to have three of your horses. The Duke himself

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: will be tomorrow at court, and they are going to meet him.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: What duke should that be comes so secretly? I hear not of him in the

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: court. Let me speak with the gentlemen. They speak English?

lines.speaker: BARDOLPH
lines.text: Ay, sir. I’ll call them to you.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: They shall have my horses, but I’ll make them pay, I’ll sauce them.

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: They have had my house a week at command; I have turned away my other

lines.speaker: HOST
lines.text: guests. They must come off, I’ll sauce them. Come.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Page, Ford, Mistress Page, Mistress Ford and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: ’Tis one of the best discretions of a ’oman as ever I did look upon.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: And did he send you both these letters at an instant?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Within a quarter of an hour.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Pardon me, wife. Henceforth, do what thou wilt.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: I rather will suspect the sun with cold

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: Than thee with wantonness. Now doth thy honour stand,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: In him that was of late an heretic,

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: As firm as faith.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: ’Tis well, ’tis well, no more.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Be not as extreme in submission as in offence.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: But let our plot go forward. Let our wives

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Yet once again, to make us public sport,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Appoint a meeting with this old fat fellow,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Where we may take him and disgrace him for it.

lines.speaker: FORD
lines.text: There is no better way than that they spoke of.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: How? To send him word they’ll meet him in the park at midnight? Fie,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: fie, he’ll never come.

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: You say he has been thrown in the rivers, and has been grievously

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: peaten as an old ’oman. Methinks there should be terrors in him, that

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: he should not come. Methinks his flesh is punished; he shall have no

lines.speaker: EVANS
lines.text: desires.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: So think I too.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Devise but how you’ll use him when he comes,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: And let us two devise to bring him thither.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: There is an old tale goes that Herne the hunter,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Sometime a keeper here in Windsor Forest,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Doth all the winter time, at still midnight,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Walk round about an oak, with great ragged horns,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And there he blasts the tree, and takes the cattle,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And makes milch-kine yield blood, and shakes a chain

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: In a most hideous and dreadful manner.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: You have heard of such a spirit, and well you know

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: The superstitious idle-headed eld

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Received and did deliver to our age,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: This tale of Herne the hunter for a truth.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Why, yet there want not many that do fear

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: In deep of night to walk by this Herne’s oak.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: But what of this?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Marry, this is our device,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: That Falstaff at that oak shall meet with us,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Disguised like Herne, with huge horns on his head.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Well, let it not be doubted but he’ll come,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: And in this shape; when you have brought him thither,

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: What shall be done with him? What is your plot?

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: That likewise have we thought upon, and thus:

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Nan Page my daughter, and my little son,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And three or four more of their growth, we’ll dress

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Like urchins, oafs and fairies, green and white,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: With rounds of waxen tapers on their heads

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And rattles in their hands. Upon a sudden,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: As Falstaff, she, and I are newly met,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Let them from forth a sawpit rush at once

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: With some diffused song; upon their sight

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: We two in great amazedness will fly.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: Then let them all encircle him about,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And fairy-like, to pinch the unclean knight,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: And ask him why, that hour of fairy revel,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: In their so sacred paths he dares to tread

lines.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
lines.text: In shape profane.

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: And till he tell the truth,

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
lines.text: Let the supposed fairies pinch him sound

lines.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
